title: Christian Surprises Muslim With Unusual Questions! Muhammed Ali
normalized_text: – How can I help you? – I've been a Christian my entire life, I was born and raised in the Adventist Christian Church; So we always went to church on Saturday, we never ate pork, we followed a lot of the Old Testament laws, but there were certain things regarding the Trinity that didn't make sense So I always had questions regarding Christianity. I wasn't firm and sure in my belief, but I did get baptised in the church at one point However, there was one day when I just sincerely asked God for guidance And I believe that He's led me towards Islam. And so today I'm coming on to take my Shahada (Testimony of Faith) – MashaAllah! (What God has willed) – I do have a few questions written down before I do that, Just so I know that if I take it, I'm not going to have any regrets. I'm going to have all my questions answered today – If you're willing to answer them? – Yes, of course, go ahead, absolutely! Ok. So the first one is in regards to how the Prophet received his Revelation. So I found that story, I believe it was in Sahih alBukhari –if I'm not mistaken– The only thing that concerns me about that, is how Angel Gabriel squeezed the Prophet three times. I just didn't understand how or why the pain was needed for him to be able to bear the Revelation! Well, there's a very basic, very simple answer, I think it's quite very logical: If you as an individual, like you are in front of me right now, OK? And you encounter me, and I am an Angel; an extraterrestrial creature that you've never seen in your life. So the minute you encounter me, you're going to be frightened. You're going to be.. This is the natural reaction of any human being that will encounter something that is not of the natural, you want to call natural norms –or whatever term you want to use– - I agree - So Prophetﷺ was in that state, he was frightened, he didn't know what he just encountered! So.. If you're just in front of me right now and I hold your shoulders like this and I press you, Wouldn't that have an effect on calming you down? – Yes or no? – Yes, I think it would Yes. So this is a very common thing that is done We see someone is confused or worried or this or that, and someone holds him and then pins him down. It's not about pain! It's about just awakening that person, and making them more assured in the state that they're in. – So does that make sense? – Yes, it does make sense I think I would just kind of compare that story to the ones I'd read in the Bible, I know the Angel Gabriel scared a lot of people in the Bible; there was even a story of someone passing out and falling on their face, but he had always told them: be not afraid, I'm from God or don't be scared. I didn't see that in the Hadith, because I saw that the Prophet Muhammadﷺ also went back to his home and asked to be covered up. So that part kind of worried me as well; if you could provide some clarification on that? Yes, as I said, first, this action of pressing is reassuring already –so he's reassuring him– That's already the number one action of reassuring him, Number two is what he said to him; like the verses that were revealed from the Quran اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ Recite in the name of your Lord (Al'alaq96:1) So he started telling him that this is now, essentially, an explanation from your Lord This is not some evil thing! It's from God: in the name of your Lord, your Maker, your Sustainer So this is a message from God as well, right? So there is another level of reassurance, but as I said, still that doesn't mean that the person is not going to have a level of shock afterward, right? After encountering the angel. But in the end, this is not the only time he encounters Angel Gabriel So you have to look throughout his life; he kept encountering Angel Gabriel, every time he got a Revelation, essentially. There are different ways he got the Revelation, but he got a lot of the Revelation from Angel Gabriel Angel Gabriel came in the form of an angel, he came in the form of a human being The Prophetﷺ: there are many ways in which he received Revelation & encountered Angel Gabriel And then he was told that he was a Prophet of God and that he had to deliver the Message This is just the initial interaction that took place OK, that makes sense. I appreciate you clarifying that for me Then my next question is; what is the concept of Salvation in Islam? Will every Muslim go to Heaven? Yes, everyone who dies on Islam will go to Paradise: this is the condition Because a lot of Christians -This is funny because you said you're from a Christian background- They say, "all Christians are going to Paradise!", "We're guaranteed Paradise!" But the thing is, it's the same thing in Christianity: you're only guaranteed Paradise if you die a Christian What if the next day you become an atheist? You're not guaranteed Paradise, are you? So, you have to die upon Christianity So in Islam, we have a promise from Allah. Allah says (AlMa'idah5:9) وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا Allah has promised those who believe There is.. وَعَدَ اللَّهُُ (It's a promise of Allah), there are many verses of the Quran where Allahﷻ says it's a promise for the Believers He has promised the believers that he will give them Paradise Now, if you die as a believer, then you are guaranteed Paradise. But you're not guaranteed to be punished before Paradise Even as a Muslim, there are still some Muslims that will be punished because you can live your life, an evil life, right? You don't have a free out-of-jail ticket, as they say. And you can do whatever you want No no, not like certain other religions. – This is not the case! – Right, right No, if you go and do evil sins and Major Sins and you don't repent, you'll be punished before you enter Paradise, you'll have to go to hellfire and.. They are purified from these sins by punishment until they enter Paradise But yes, everyone who dies upon the testimony of faith, believing in it, is going to enter Paradise OK, that makes sense. That also makes more sense in my mind, just from a Christian's perspective of just believing in Jesus Christ and then you're automatically going to go to Heaven, no matter what you've done! You have salvation because of the crucifixion on the cross. So, that makes sense The third question ties into what I just asked, and it's the concept of good versus bad deeds being weighed on the day of judgment So if you die on Islam, if you die as a Muslim, you said that you will enter Heaven But why do your good vs bad deeds have to be weighed, and you got 10 more good deeds to enter Heaven? It is exactly what I was telling you; the fact that some Muslims will be punished. So if their bad deeds outweigh their good deeds, that means they still are going to be punished before they enter Paradise because they didn't live.. -They didn't do as best as they could in this life- No one is going to be perfect, Allah doesn't ask you to be perfect, but he asks you to do as much as you can And Allah makes it super easy for you, actually! One good deed, you get 10 times the reward in Islam. To 700, to an unlimited amount, if Allah wants to increase you, depending on your intention Maybe Allah see you one day: one person, he had only two pounds, and he was hungry, and he brought bread, and he gave it to someone else! And he has no money, as he has only that two pounds! And Allah; for that very small deed that if I were to do and I have millions, I'm not going to get the same reward, because of the situation, because of the circumstances, and all of that. So Allah can give him a reward that we cannot even imagine, because of that simple action That's why in Islam, you have an example of a woman who was a prostitute, And there was a thirsty dog in the desert, and she was going by a well, and his tongue was out because he was thirsty, he's going to die from thirst. And then she went in, she used her shoes, and she gave him water, and then Allah forgave her for that. She lived a sinful life –if you can use the term "Sinful life"– But still, she was forgiven because of that specific action she did So in Islam, Allah makes it super easy for you for that reason. In Islam, there are Minor Sins and Major Sins. For the Major Sins, you have to seek repentance, but for the Minor Sins, if you do good deeds, Allah forgives them. Allah says (Hud11:114) إِنَّ ٱلْحَسَنَـٰتِ يُذْهِبْنَ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ Good deeds remove bad deeds Without you even asking for anything, you just do good deeds and Allah removes from the bad deeds that you have Allah gives you chances and opportunities when you go to Hajj حج (Pilgrimage), and then he forgives all these sins if you do a correct Pilgrimage He gives you Ramadan; he forgives all your past sins, if you fast Ramadan correctly, or you pray in Ramadan.. All of these things! Allah makes it so easy for the people But still, there will be some Muslims -some of us- who are not good, not taking that, even though it's so easy. We're not taking this handout -if you use that term- from Allahﷻ, we're still living a bad life, and in the end, our bad deeds will outweigh our good deeds, and we'll be punished for a period of time -if we're Muslims- You're going to be punished for a period of time, and then you're going to enter Paradise. Because accountability is not for disbelievers anyway.. if you are a disbeliever, you go to Hellfire straight away, there is no point of accountability This accountability is for the Muslims. Yes, that seems like the Christian concept, even though it's not followed: "Faith is dead without works" (James2:17) So it seems like, you're saying that: whenever you have true faith, as a Muslim, you're going to automatically do good deeds, you're going to do good works, You're going to pray, go to Hajj (pilgrimage) as you said, charity, whatever it may be, that's just going to come naturally Yes, external actions reflect internal beliefs. That's always the case! If you love someone, you'll behave like you love them. You know, when they're in need, you're going to help them The actions show everything. That's why when people get married; every day he says to his wife or she says to him "I love you" And then they're fighting every two minutes! They have issues. You can say words, But is it really manifested in the behaviour and actions you're taking with the other individual? That's the true testimony of the faith. So in Islam, faith is that: it's testimony of the tongue, belief in the heart, and actions. These three things have to be present OK. Yes, that makes perfect sense. My last question is in regard to the Qareen I believe I'm saying that right. Hopefully, I'm not butchering it too bad – The قَرين (Qareen), OK. You're not, you're doing good – Yes, sir In Sahih Muslim, Book:39, Hadith:6757, it says: (Allah helped the Prophet convert one of the Qareen to become a Muslim) And then it said (the Qareen commanded him to do good things.) So maybe I'm reading too much into that, but it kind of sounds like perhaps he was taking commands and orders! How is it translated? أنَّ اللَّهَ أعانَنِي عَلَيهِ فأسْلَمَ. How is it translated though, in the one you're reading? I just had not written it down, but I can try to pull it up on my phone and get you it Yes, OK. I'll explain it to you anyway -because sometimes this translation can be different translations- but أسلم there means he submitted. So the Qareen submitted to the Prophetﷺ. Because the Qareen's job.. – You're searching for it, right? – Yes, sir – Yes, I'll let you find it – So I can have it. OK I want to see what the translation that you're reading says as well. OK, this is Sahih Muslim, Book:39, Hadith number 6757. It says: Abdullah bin Mas'ood -not sure about that pronunciation- reported that Allah's Messengerﷺ said: (There is none amongst you with whom is not an attack from amongst the Jinn (Devil), They (The Companions) said, Allah's Messenger with you too? Thereupon he said: Yes, but Allah helps me against him, and so I'm safe from his hand and he does not command me, but for good). OK. So I got this then. OK. So here, yes. First, it says that Allahﷻ have aided him; أنَّ اللَّهَ أعانَنِي عَلَيهِ فأسْلَمَ, Allahﷻ aided the Prophetﷺ against the Qareen Now, when it says, commands me to do good here, it's referring to the Qareen actually, it's not referring to the Prophet, but the explanation is this: what is the job of a Qareen from an Islamic point of view? The job of a Qareen from an Islamic point of view is to whisper evil things to the believers So every human being has a Qareen, and that Qareen's job is to whisper evil deeds to the Muslims Whatever these evil ideas that you're getting, you're just sitting down normally in a day and you start giving bad thoughts, evil ideas, bad doubts, whatever term people want to use, It's from the Qareen, it's from the شيطان (Shaytan) because the Qareen is a Shaytan (Satan) So, this is the job of a Qareen In this case, Allahﷻ aided the Prophetﷺ against his Qareen, and then "Aslama" means he submitted. So he submitted to the Prophetﷺ And some other scholars would say he became a believer; because we believe the Qareen is a Jinn, and the Jinn; There are Muslims from the Jinn and there are Disbelievers from the Jinn. There are two ways to understand. You can either understand "Aslama" means he submitted to the Prophet's command, he became a Submitter to the Prophet, or that he became a Believer So when it says he commands me to do good, that means.. if he ever gives you ideas or whispers, it's a good thing Now, so opposite to him telling you: OK, for example, steal from this person, curse this person, this person is evil, he's actually going to remind you of good or tell you good things, right? Give charity, do this, that. The exact opposite.. of what the Qareen would say in the case of being evil, essentially! OK, so since the Prophet was so righteous or he was the last Messenger, He, with the help of Allah, was able to convert the Qareen – So he only told him to do good things, or..? – Yes – That makes sense – Yes So the Qareen only says good things, basically. Good ideas are coming And you have these movie kind of concepts of you have two angels.. or one evil angel and one good angel on the two shoulders – You have probably seen this – Yes One is supposed to do good and one is supposed to do evil. This is a close analogy really to it! Whispering good -in the sense of telling you to do good- rather than telling you to do evil All right, yeah. That's the concept I was thinking in my head when I was trying to imagine it, yes All right. That's all the questions I have. So, I'm definitely ready to take my Shahada and move forward. OK, Alhamdulillah الحمد لله (All praise is due to God). All right. We'll do it InshaAllah إن شاء الله (If God wills it). We'll do it first in English and then we'll do it in Arabic, OK? – OK. – All right. So let's say first in English. Say: I testify that there's nothing worthy of worship except Allah, and I testify that Prophet Muhammad is His Messenger and Servant. Excellent. Now we'll say the same thing in Arabic, say; أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلَّا الله وَأشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ الله MashaAllah ما شاء الله (God has willed it), that's it, brother. – Thank you, brother – Alhamdulillah, that's it. SubhanAllah سبحان الله (Glorified is God). You were there probably at the backstage when I said to the other brother– the keys to entering Paradise, isn't it? This is the way for someone to enter Paradise. And Allahﷻ forgives you past sins and mistakes But SubhanAllah, I'm very happy to see someone your age doing the research, I'm happy to see this! In this day and age; you've got a lot of the youth in the West completely misguided They don't know whether they're a man or a woman or a potato or a helicopter, – Right! right! – You know? Wearing animal costumes and jumping in classrooms.. So it's always good to see someone who is at that age doing research, looking for the Truth Do you understand me? And looking for what is the Truth, and leaving falsehood. Choosing to leave falsehood! Even though he's born upon falsehood in his family or teaching him Christianity, or whatever! And he still chooses: OK, I researched, this is not the Truth, I'm going to leave it. And then look for the Truth, and then adopt the Truth So may Allahﷻ keep you firm on the Truth. And as I said to the other person; please send me your details To my email.. Did you write down the email? – I don't know if you did, or not. – I didn't know. Let me write it down real quick Yes, so this is the email. – It is the channel name.. – Oh, pretty simple. – Yes. – Yes, pretty simple. You can send me InshAllah an email with your information, and I'll connect you InshAllah with our team as well to mentor you and anything like that. And then you can also ask me if you need to ask something on the email InshAllah. And I will make sure InshAllah to get back to you. OK, brother Isaiah, it was a pleasure talking to you. Do you have any other questions? Yes, go ahead.. I just want to say quickly that it's been, obviously, heavy on my heart for a while, It's been around a year of study, There was even a time for about two weeks; I was praying all five daily prayers And so, I've really tried to sincerely go about this and study, you know, right now I'm reading the Quran, the Book of Monotheism.. So, I appreciate you answering all my questions, and if you and everyone else could keep me in their Du'aa دعاء (Supplication) because –like I said-' I do have a Christian family. So, it's going to be a little bit difficult, but yes.. May Allahﷻ make it easy for you. And I'm very happy for you, brother. May Allahﷻ keep you firm in the Truth and accept from you, your effort. And -when people accept Islam- this is always way better. After research and this and that, they're firm, they understand what they're doing, why they're doing it. May Allahﷻ bless you, brother. – OK, I'll let you go, brother Isaiah. – OK, thank you so much. Bye-bye Assalamu 'alaykum (May peace be upon you) See you, brother
